The first idea we use to convey Green’s Theorem quantifies the rate at which a floating paddle wheel, with axis perpendicular to the plane, spins at a point in a fluid flowing in a plane region. This idea gives some sense of how the fluid is circulating around axes located at different points and perpendicular to the region. Physicists sometimes refer to this as the circulation density of a vector field F at a point. To obtain it, we consider the velocity field
F(x, y) = M(x, y)i + N(x, y)j
and the rectangle A in Figure 16.26 (where we assume both components of F are positive).
